subject: Elden Ring, Godrick the Grafted, locked on, player one-handed straight sword

method.extraction: ffmpeg -vf select='not(mod(n,60))',drawgrid=w=iw/8:h=ih/8 — one frame per second, overlaid with an 8x8 grid so NDC can be read off the gridlines (gridline k from the left is NDC x = -1 + k/4; from the top, NDC y = 1 - k/4).
method.reading: Anchors read by eye against the gridlines: P_a = the player's chest/spine2, T_a = the boss's chest mass, T_h = the boss's head. Precision is about a fifth of a grid cell, i.e. +/-0.05 NDC. This is a MEASUREMENT OFF A REFERENCE, not a frame-exact extraction, and it is recorded as such — it is used to check the SIGN and the BAND of our own framing, never to set a constant.
method.limitation: 5 sampled frames of 1039. A larger sample would tighten the bands; it would not change the four conclusions, each of which is a qualitative fact visible in every frame.

conclusions.finding: Both anchors are on screen in 5 of 5 sampled frames, at every range including the closest.
conclusions.consequence: The bars are the right shape. Nothing to change.

conclusions.finding: The PLAYER anchor sits low: NDC y between -0.40 and -0.75, and at the closest range it is at or past -0.70. It is therefore OUTSIDE the +/-0.70 safe rect for a large part of a big-boss fight, while remaining comfortably on screen — and the upstream camera does NOT extend its boom to bring it back inside.
conclusions.bears_on: RI-CAM03 §C step 5, which extends the arm +0.150 m/frame whenever EITHER anchor is outside the safe rect
conclusions.consequence: BINDING ON THIS BUILD. A literal reading of step 5 makes the arm ratchet to the 7.50 m cap for the whole fight — which is RI-CAM03's own 'How we lose' #5, the strategy-game camera. §C's priority order already says safe-rect containment is priority (4) and the two on-screen guarantees are (1) and (2); this build implements step 5 driven by ON-SCREEN loss first, with the safe rect as a bounded secondary that cannot ratchet. See sim/camera.js containment().

conclusions.finding: The TARGET chest sits high — NDC y +0.30 to +0.60, i.e. roughly 20-35% of screen height measured from the top.
conclusions.bears_on: [CMB06] vertical framing band, 'target chest between 38% and 62% of screen height', and RI-CAM03 §E's >= 0.900 bar on it
conclusions.consequence: Against an 8 m boss the reference sits ABOVE the 38-62% band, because §D's size_bias tilts the camera up. The 38-62% band is a HUMAN-TARGET bar and this build measures it as one; reporting it against a great boss and calling it a failure would be measuring the size term and calling it a defect.

conclusions.finding: The boss's head leaves the top of the frame at close range in 4 of 5 samples.
conclusions.bears_on: RI-CAM03 §D 'the documented degradation' — for h >= 6.0 m at d < 4.0 m, T_h may leave the frame
conclusions.consequence: Confirmed against the reference. The degradation is real upstream behaviour and the >= 0.880 T_h bar for large targets is calibrated to it, not a concession.

conclusions.finding: Both anchors stay near the vertical midline: |NDC x| <= 0.15 in every sample.
conclusions.bears_on: RI-CAM01 §A's reduced locked shoulder offset (+0.26 m rather than +0.42 m)
conclusions.consequence: Corroborates the reduction: a large lateral bias under lock would push one anchor toward a frame edge, and the reference shows almost no lateral spread.
